# dsh-noagent-schedule
[](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-noagent-schedule/blob/main/LICENSE) [](https://github.com/mon
key-sking/dsh-noagent-schedule/commits/main) [](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-noagent-schedule
/search?l=JavaScript) [](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-noagent-schedule/releases) [](https://g
ithub.com/monkey-sking/dsh-noagent-schedule/stargazers) [](https://github.com/monkey-sking/dsh-noage
nt-schedule/network/members)
**Run shell scripts on a schedule inside DeepSeek Harness — with no model call and no token cost.**

Every scheduling plugin in the DSH ecosystem delivers a message to a session or starts a new one,
so

a cron tick always means a model wake-up. This plugin takes the other path: the Host runs the
comma

nd itself, the way `systemd` or `launchd` would. The model is only involved when you actually
want i
t to be — see wake on change.
简体中文
## What it gives you
| **Zero token** | A tick that runs a script costs nothing. The plugin never touches the LLM service

s. |
| **Cron or interval** | Five-field Vixie cron (`*/15 9-17 * * 1-5`, `sun..sat`, `jan..dec`) or

`everySeconds`. |
| **Explicit time zones** | IANA zones per job, so the schedule means what it say

s regardless of where the Host runs. |
| **Logs you can read** | One file per run with argv, exit co

de, stdout and stderr; a `runs.jsonl` ledger beside it. |
| **Overlap protection** | A job whose pre

vious run is still going is skipped, not stacked. |
| **Timeout** | Oversized jobs are terminated at

`timeoutSeconds`. |
| **Qinglong-style task page** (open it from the sidebar; not duplicated in Set
tings) | Overview cards, search and status filter, one row per job with a status dot, a human-readab
le schedule ("daily 18:30" instead of `30 18 * * *`), last and next run, a strip of the last 8 resul

ts, and a log drawer. |
| **Edit from the page** | Enable or disable a job, change its cron or inter
val, timeout, name or command, and delete it. Every write is validated, backed up, and re-parsed bef

ore it lands, so `jobs.json` can never be left unloadable. |
| **Agent tools** | `noagent_status`, `

noagent_run`, `noagent_log`, `noagent_update` — the same operations the UI uses. |
| **Wake on chang
e** | Turn a polling script into an event source: the model is woken only when its output changes. |

## Where things live
| | Default | Configure |

| Job list | `~/.dsh/noagent/jobs.json` | `jobsFile` |
| State and logs | `~/.dsh/noagent/state/` |

`~/.dsh/noagent/jobs.json` | `jobsFile` |

The job file is re-read every 10 seconds, so adding, editing or disabling a job needs no restart.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Jobs
[代码示例省略，未执行]
| Field | Meaning |

| `id` | Unique, also the log directory name. Required. |
| `cron` | Five fields: minute hour day-of

-month month day-of-week. Supports `*/n`, `a-b`, `a-b/n`, lists, `sun..sat`, `jan..dec`. |
| `everyS

econds` | Fixed interval, minimum 30. Use instead of `cron`. |
| `timeZone` | IANA zone. Defaults to

the plugin's `defaultTimeZone`. |
| `cwd` | Working directory. Defaults to the user's home. |
| `co

mmand` | Run through `/bin/bash -lc`. Alternatively use `argv` for an exact process. |
| `argv` | Ar

ray form; no shell involved. |
| `env` | Extra environment variables, merged over the inherited envi

ronment. |
| `timeoutSeconds` | Terminate after this long. Default 300. |
| `enabled` | `false` keep

s the job in the file but does not schedule it. |
| `wakeOnChange` | See below. |
### Why `bash -lc`

A GUI-launched Host inherits a minimal `PATH` — often just `/usr/bin:/bin`. A login shell picks up
t

he user's profile, so `git`, `node`, `python3` and friends resolve the way they do in a terminal.
Ho
mebrew's standard prefixes are prepended as a fallback.
If you would rather not depend on shell startup files, use `argv` with absolute paths.
## Wake on change

A polling script usually answers one question: *did anything change?* Running it on a timer is
free;
waking a model to ask the same question every few minutes is not.
`wakeOnChange` separates the two:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
How it behaves:

- The probe runs every 120 seconds. **No change means no model call at all.**
- Output is normalised

(lines matching `ignoreLines` are dropped), then fingerprinted.
- A changed fingerprint schedules a

one-shot delivery to `sessionId` about a second later, carrying
the probe output through `{{output}

}`.
- The first run only records a baseline, so installing the plugin does not immediately wake anyo

ne.
Set `notifyOnFirstRun: true` to opt in.
- A non-zero exit is never treated as "something changed

" — failures show up in the log and the
status, not as false wakes.
- Every wake is a one-shot sched

uled delivery, and one-shot rows stay in the Host's task table
after delivery. The plugin deletes ea

ch wake row once it has been delivered (the previous row is
removed before the next wake, delivered

rows are swept every 30 seconds, and leftovers from an
earlier version are cleaned on the first tick

), so "automation tasks" keeps listing only the real
recurring jobs instead of a wall of identical o

ne-shot entries.
- Empty output means nothing to report.
- `onlyOnNew` can be narrowed with `keyPatt

ern`: only the matched part of each line identifies an
entry, so a conversation whose last message c

hanges (including our own reply) is not "new"; only a
genuinely new conversation wakes the session.

Lines unmatched by the pattern fall back to the
whole line.
